ceo_directive_round_257: P0: collision-search 3 structures. P1: add INFORMATION ACCESS NOVELTY gate. P2: new information channel, not better sensor. P3: only after Level-2 novelty.

IB-01_implant_micromotion.name: Implant Micromotion Measurement via Impedance
IB-01_implant_micromotion.hidden_variable: In-vivo implant micromotion under physiological load

prior_art_found.source: Vibration analysis for implant loosening detection
prior_art_found.what_it_does: Uses external vibration excitation + acoustic/response measurement to detect loosening. Research since 1980s (e.g., Varini et al., Georgiou et al.). Measures implant-bone interface stiffness non-invasively.
prior_art_found.covers_micromotion: Indirectly — loosening IS excessive micromotion. But this is EPISODIC (clinic visit) not CONTINUOUS.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Research implants with embedded strain gauges, accelerometers, or pressure sensors. E.g., Bergmann et al. (Charité) have instrumented hip implants measuring load, temperature, friction since 1990s.
prior_art_found.covers_micromotion: NO — these measure LOAD and CONTACT PRESSURE, not micromotion (relative displacement between implant and bone).
prior_art_found.resolution: N/A for micromotion (measures force, not displacement).

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Passive RFID tags on implants whose resonant frequency shifts with interface stiffness changes (loosening). Research papers exist.
prior_art_found.covers_micromotion: Indirectly — frequency shift correlates with loosening. But it's a BINARY indicator (loose/not-loose), not a QUANTITATIVE micromotion measurement.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Piezoelectric materials in implants for energy harvesting + sensing. Measures strain/vibration, not implant-bone relative motion.
prior_art_found.covers_micromotion: NO — measures implant strain, not implant-bone interface motion.

information_access_novelty_gate.observable_today: Implant loosening can be detected EPISODICALLY via: (1) X-ray (radiation, ~0.1mm resolution, static), (2) CT (radiation, ~0.05mm, static), (3) vibration analysis (non-invasive, ~10-100 microns, episodic), (4) clinical symptoms (late, qualitative). Continuous in-vivo micromotion is NOT observable.
information_access_novelty_gate.resolution_today: X-ray: ~100 microns. CT: ~50 microns. Vibration: ~10-100 microns. Clinical: qualitative only.
information_access_novelty_gate.sampling_frequency_today: Episodic (per clinic visit, typically 6-12 months). NO continuous monitoring.
information_access_novelty_gate.invasiveness_today: X-ray/CT: radiation exposure. Vibration: non-invasive but requires clinic visit. Clinical: non-invasive but late.
information_access_novelty_gate.new_mechanism_resolution: Impedance-based: potentially sub-micron (impedance is sensitive to small geometric changes).
information_access_novelty_gate.new_mechanism_invasiveness: Zero additional invasiveness (sensor is IN the implant, no external measurement needed).
information_access_novelty_gate.new_mechanism_cost: Sensor integration cost (~$10-$50 per implant) + reader. No per-measurement cost.

quantified_advantage.frequency_improvement: Continuous vs episodic (6-12 months) — INFINITE improvement in temporal resolution

IB-01_implant_micromotion.is_this_a_new_information_channel: PARTIALLY. The variable (micromotion) is known to be important. The MEASUREMENT METHOD (impedance-based continuous monitoring) is different from existing methods (X-ray, CT, vibration). But impedance sensing itself is known (cemetery CE-001 used impedance for hydraulic state estimation in eShunt). The question is whether applying impedance to implant-bone interface micromotion is novel.
IB-01_implant_micromotion.what_would_make_it_genuinely_novel: If the impedance-micromotion relationship requires a NEW PHYSICAL MODEL — e.g., a model connecting impedance change at the implant-bone interface to micromotion that is not derivable from standard electromagnetic theory. If it's just 'measure impedance and correlate with loosening,' it's engineering. If the transduction mechanism (impedance → micromotion) involves a non-obvious physical insight, it may be novel.
IB-01_implant_micromotion.novelty_reason: Impedance sensing of implant interfaces exists in research (RFID loosening detection). The continuous + quantitative micromotion aspect is not directly covered, but the APPROACH (impedance for loosening) is known. This is 'better sensor for known variable' rather than 'new information channel.' Level 1, not Level 2.
IB-01_implant_micromotion.verdict: RESET — does not pass INFORMATION ACCESS NOVELTY gate at Level 2. The approach (impedance for implant loosening) is known. The improvement (continuous + quantitative) is engineering, not invention.

IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.name: Tissue Drug Concentration via Implantable Microdialysis
IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.hidden_variable: Real-time drug concentration at target tissue (not blood)
IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.proposed_mechanism: Implantable microdialysis probe with continuous wireless measurement

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Implantable subcutaneous sensors measuring ISF glucose continuously (Dexcom, Abbott Freestyle Libre, Medtronic Guardian). THE dominant example of continuous tissue-level monitoring.
prior_art_found.covers_drug_concentration: NO — measures GLUCOSE specifically (enzymatic electrochemical). Not generalizable to arbitrary drugs.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Bedside microdialysis probes (CMA/Mdialysis) used in neurointensive care to measure brain tissue metabolites (glucose, lactate, pyruvate, glycerol) continuously. FDA-cleared (Mdialysis 70 CNS System).
prior_art_found.covers_drug_concentration: PARTIALLY — measures small metabolites, NOT drugs. But the MICRODIALYSIS METHOD is established for continuous tissue monitoring.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Research on electrochemical sensors for specific drugs (e.g., lithium, phenytoin, doxorubicin). Typically ex-vivo or short-term in-vivo.
prior_art_found.covers_drug_concentration: PARTIALLY — demonstrates that electrochemical drug sensing is possible, but for specific drugs, not generalizable.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Research on implantable sensors for ISF drug levels (e.g., Miller et al. for chemotherapy drugs). Typically preclinical.
prior_art_found.covers_drug_concentration: YES — directly covers the concept of implantable continuous drug monitoring in ISF.

information_access_novelty_gate.observable_today: Blood drug levels (invasive, episodic). Tissue drug levels via biopsy (invasive, episodic). ISF glucose via CGM (continuous, but glucose only). Brain metabolites via clinical microdialysis (continuous, but metabolites only, not drugs).
information_access_novelty_gate.resolution_today: Blood: micromolar. Biopsy: nanomolar. CGM: ~1 mg/dL (glucose only).
information_access_novelty_gate.sampling_frequency_today: Blood: episodic (per draw). Biopsy: episodic. CGM: continuous (glucose). Clinical microdialysis: continuous (metabolites).
information_access_novelty_gate.invasiveness_today: Blood: venipuncture. Biopsy: invasive (needle/surgical). CGM: subcutaneous needle. Microdialysis: catheter implantation.
information_access_novelty_gate.cost_today: Blood draws: $50-$200. Biopsy: $500-$5000. CGM: $300/month. Clinical microdialysis: $2000+/day (neuro-ICU).

quantified_advantage.frequency_improvement: Continuous vs episodic blood draws — major improvement.
quantified_advantage.invasiveness_improvement: Comparable to CGM (subcutaneous). Less invasive than biopsy.
quantified_advantage.cost_improvement: Lower than biopsy or neuro-ICU microdialysis.

IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.is_this_a_new_information_channel: NO. Continuous tissue monitoring via microdialysis EXISTS (clinical cerebral microdialysis). Continuous drug monitoring via ISF sensors EXISTS in research (Miller et al.). The proposed mechanism is 'apply existing microdialysis/electrochemical sensing to a broader set of drugs.' That is APPLICATION, not a new channel.
IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.what_would_make_it_genuinely_novel: If the mechanism enables measurement of a drug class that CANNOT currently be measured by electrochemical methods — e.g., a new transduction mechanism for non-electroactive drugs. Or if it enables measurement at a tissue site that is currently inaccessible (e.g., intratumoral with wireless readout). But 'implantable microdialysis for drug monitoring' is known.
IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.novelty_reason: Continuous tissue monitoring exists (clinical microdialysis). Continuous drug monitoring exists in research. The proposed mechanism is application of known methods to broader drug classes. Not a new information channel. Level 1.
IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.verdict: RESET — does not pass INFORMATION ACCESS NOVELTY gate. Continuous tissue monitoring already exists (CGM for glucose, clinical microdialysis for metabolites). The improvement (broader drug classes) is engineering, not invention.

IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.name: Vessel Wall Shear Stress at Implant Interface
IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.hidden_variable: Local wall shear stress at the implant-tissue interface
IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.proposed_mechanism: Implant-surface-integrated pressure sensors measuring local shear directly

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Pressure wires (e.g., Abbott PressureWire, Philips Wire) measure intravascular pressure for FFR (Fractional Flow Reserve). FDA-cleared, widely used.
prior_art_found.covers_shear_stress: NO — measures PRESSURE, not shear stress. FFR uses pressure ratio, not shear.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Intravascular imaging for plaque morphology, vessel dimensions. Can estimate flow via contrast tracking.
prior_art_found.covers_shear_stress: Indirectly — can COMPUTE shear stress from flow estimates. But requires invasive catheterization, not implant-based, and is episodic.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Computational fluid dynamics on patient-specific vascular geometry (from CT/MRI) estimates wall shear stress.
prior_art_found.covers_shear_stress: YES — computes shear stress, but from MODEL not MEASUREMENT. Requires assumptions about flow, viscosity, geometry. Not direct measurement.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Research on stents with embedded pressure/flow sensors for restenosis monitoring. E.g., wireless stent sensors measuring neointimal growth via pressure changes.
prior_art_found.covers_shear_stress: NO — measures pressure/flow, not shear stress directly. Pressure changes detect restenosis, not local shear.

prior_art_found.what_it_does: Academic research on shear stress effects on endothelium. Typically in-vitro (flow chambers) or computational. No in-vivo continuous direct measurement.
prior_art_found.covers_shear_stress: Measures shear in VITRO, not in vivo. No clinical device directly measures wall shear stress at implant interface.

information_access_novelty_gate.observable_today: Wall shear stress is COMPUTED (via CFD from CT/MRI) or ESTIMATED (via IVUS flow tracking). NO direct continuous in-vivo measurement at implant interface exists.
information_access_novelty_gate.resolution_today: CFD: ~0.01 Pa (computed, model-dependent). IVUS: ~0.1-1 Pa (estimated). In-vivo direct: NOT AVAILABLE.
information_access_novelty_gate.sampling_frequency_today: CFD: episodic (per simulation). IVUS: episodic (per catheterization). Continuous: NOT AVAILABLE.
information_access_novelty_gate.invasiveness_today: CFD: non-invasive (but computed, not measured). IVUS: invasive (catheterization).
information_access_novelty_gate.new_mechanism_resolution: Direct measurement: potentially ~0.001 Pa (surface-integrated sensor at interface).
information_access_novelty_gate.new_mechanism_invasiveness: Zero additional invasiveness (sensor is ON the implant surface).
information_access_novelty_gate.new_mechanism_cost: Sensor integration cost (~$10-$100 per implant). No per-measurement cost.

quantified_advantage.resolution_improvement: 10-1000x better than CFD estimates (direct measurement vs model computation).
quantified_advantage.frequency_improvement: Continuous vs episodic (per simulation/catheterization) — INFINITE improvement.
quantified_advantage.invasiveness_improvement: Zero additional invasiveness (sensor on implant) vs IVUS catheterization.
quantified_advantage.cost_improvement: ~$10-$100 per implant vs $3000-$10000 per IVUS procedure.
quantified_advantage.key_advantage: DIRECT measurement vs CFD COMPUTATION. This is not 'better sensor for known variable' — it is 'first direct measurement of a variable that was previously only computable from models.'

IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.is_this_a_new_information_channel: POTENTIALLY YES. Wall shear stress at the implant-tissue interface is currently only COMPUTED (CFD) or ESTIMATED (IVUS), never DIRECTLY MEASURED in vivo continuously. A surface-integrated sensor that directly measures local shear stress at the exact implant-tissue interface would provide a NEW information channel: the first direct, continuous, in-vivo measurement of local hemodynamic stress at the interface where thrombosis occurs.
IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.what_would_make_it_genuinely_novel: If the transduction mechanism (surface pressure → shear stress) requires a NEW physical model — e.g., a micro-fabricated shear sensor that measures tangential force directly (not inferred from pressure differential). If the sensor measures shear DIRECTLY (not inferring from pressure/flow), that is a new measurement capability. The key question: is direct shear measurement at a vascular implant surface technically feasible and non-obvious?
IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.novelty_reason: No prior art directly measures wall shear stress at the implant-tissue interface continuously in vivo. Existing methods compute (CFD) or estimate (IVUS) shear, but do not MEASURE it directly at the interface. Smart stents measure pressure/flow (not shear). Endothelial shear research is in-vitro/computational. The gap is genuine: direct continuous in-vivo shear measurement at implant surface. Level 2 — survives initial collision, needs deeper §103.
IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.verdict: SURVIVES — passes INFORMATION ACCESS NOVELTY gate at Level 2. Direct continuous in-vivo wall shear stress measurement at implant interface is NOT available today (only computed via CFD or estimated via IVUS). This is potentially a new information channel, not just 'better sensor for known variable.'

p2_information_channel_assessment.the_distinction: A 'better sensor for known variable' is engineering (Level 1). A 'new information channel' is potentially invention (Level 2+). The test: does the mechanism provide access to information that existing 2026 technology CANNOT obtain with comparable fidelity, continuity, invasiveness, cost, or temporal resolution?

IB-01_implant_micromotion.reason: Micromotion is measurable today (X-ray, CT, vibration). The improvement is resolution + continuity, but the INFORMATION CHANNEL (implant-bone interface motion) is known and accessible. This is 'better sensor.'

IB-02_tissue_drug_concentration.reason: Tissue drug concentration is measurable today (biopsy, clinical microdialysis). The improvement is broader drug classes + continuity, but the INFORMATION CHANNEL (tissue chemical concentration) is known and accessible. This is 'better sensor.'

IB-03_vessel_wall_shear_stress.reason: Wall shear stress at implant interface is NOT directly measurable today — only computable (CFD) or estimable (IVUS). A direct continuous in-vivo measurement at the implant surface would be a NEW information channel: first access to a variable that was previously only modeled, never measured.

p2_information_channel_assessment.summary: Only IB-03 (vessel wall shear stress) survives as a potential new information channel. The key distinction: IB-01 and IB-02 improve existing measurement capabilities (better resolution, continuity, convenience). IB-03 provides access to information that is currently UNOBSERVABLE (only computable from models).

summary.IB-01: RESET — Level 1. Micromotion is measurable today (X-ray, CT, vibration). Better sensor, not new channel.
summary.IB-02: RESET — Level 1. Tissue drug concentration is measurable today (biopsy, clinical microdialysis). Better sensor, not new channel.
summary.IB-03: SURVIVES — Level 2. Wall shear stress at implant interface is NOT directly measurable today (only computed via CFD, estimated via IVUS). Potentially a NEW information channel.
summary.key_finding: Only 1 of 3 structures survives the information-access novelty gate. IB-03 (vessel wall shear stress) is the first candidate to reach Level 2 novelty because it provides access to a variable that is currently UNOBSERVABLE (only computable from models), not merely 'better measurement of a known variable.' This is the distinction between 'new information channel' (potentially invention) and 'better sensor' (engineering).
ib03_next_steps: Deeper §103: search for direct shear measurement in any context (not just vascular implants)
Determine if the transduction mechanism (surface sensor → shear stress) requires a new physical model
Assess if direct shear measurement at vascular implant surface is technically feasible
Only after Level 2 confirmed: buyer economics → build-vs-buy → killer experiment
summary.honest_caveat: IB-03's Level 2 is based on training knowledge through early 2025. The collision search found NO prior art for direct continuous in-vivo wall shear measurement at implant surfaces, but this must be verified with live web search for 2025-2026 publications. If a shear sensor implant exists, IB-03 is downgraded to Level 0.
